# Data gathering

> The most efficient way to gather data in general, information foraging first: foraging models, the stopping estimator for what is still unseen, the choice of the next source as a bandit, and the value of information for a dear source, as programs the reviews can run. First review written: foraging and stopping, ending on a named baseline for the stopping rule, with a program that estimates the unseen from a search log.

Each page's markdown source is served at the same path with a .md extension. This index is written by hand; AGENTS.md says to keep it in step.

## The repository

- [Data gathering](https://tewf.github.io/ai-augmented-data-gathering/README.md): the scope, the first job and the questions its review must answer
- [Decisions](https://tewf.github.io/ai-augmented-data-gathering/decisions/README.md): one record per choice that shapes the repository

## The review

- [Evidence](https://tewf.github.io/ai-augmented-data-gathering/evidence/README.md): the review and the bibliography of every work it cites
- [Foraging and stopping](https://tewf.github.io/ai-augmented-data-gathering/evidence/foraging-and-stopping/README.md): a first pass of 40 sources, in the five steps of a thesis review
- [Baseline](https://tewf.github.io/ai-augmented-data-gathering/evidence/foraging-and-stopping/baseline.md): coverage stopping with Chao1, compared with the rule of five results with no new concept
- [On the family](https://tewf.github.io/ai-augmented-data-gathering/evidence/foraging-and-stopping/on-the-family.md): the estimator run on three protocols, and what a search log must hold
